requirements.requirement: On node1, record sudo-invoked commands in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A valid system-wide sudoers policy directs logging to the required file. Direct observations show multiple sudo commands recorded with timestamps, invoking user “antrieb,” run-as user, working directory, and command; fresh behavior also worked after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system logs.
requirements.summary: The policy disables sudo syslog command logging, and unique command markers generated both before and after reboot appeared in the dedicated log while searches of auth.log and syslog returned zero matches.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations consistently show Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic. The solution uses the installed sudo 1.8.16 facility, parses successfully, and remains functional after reboot; no package installation or platform replacement is shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and coherent: it captures a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered rsyslog, sudo policy, historical audit data, and fresh isolated logging. The only notable hygiene issue is one small verification file left in /tmp.
limitations: Testing used representative unique markers rather than attempting every possible sudo invocation form; the valid global sudoers policy and multiple observed commands provide strong supporting coverage.
The post-executor lifecycle snapshot does not inventory the sudoers drop-in or dedicated log itself, so their final state relies on the direct post-reboot executor observation.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material mutations had clear roles: the sudoers drop-in established the required policy, marker files tested behavior, and the reboot command executed the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. The pre-reboot marker and reboot log were removed by the reboot, but the necessary post-reboot verification left /tmp/post-reboot-sudo-audit behind; this is minor executor-caused residue. No failed services, new listeners, or package damage were observed.
